body: I don't know if there's a way to run OpenAI Codex in a headless way from the CLI right now. Do you know it to be the case? I agree that it would be great if we can allow all different types of agents to run.
yes, you can use `codex exec`. More info [here](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference#codex-exec)

There's `codex exec` for that.

https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference/#codex-exec

Essentially, it's `codex exec [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]`, with either a string for the prompt, or if `-` is used), instructions are read from stdin.

The **“Ralph Wiggum method”** (also called the **Ralph Wiggum technique or Ralph loop**) isn’t a traditional academic method — it’s a **recent AI development technique** named humorously after *Ralph Wiggum*, the lovable, persistent, and often clueless character from *The Simpsons*. ([[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Wiggum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][1])

### 📌 What It Is

The Ralph Wiggum method is an **iterative AI agent workflow** that keeps an AI model working on a task **in a loop** until it truly completes it, rather than stopping after just one attempt. In essence: you **feed the same prompt repeatedly in a controlled loop**, and the agent refines its output each time until it meets your specified success criteria. ([[Medium](https://jpcaparas.medium.com/ralph-wiggum-explained-the-claude-code-loop-that-keeps-going-3250dcc30809?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][2])

> The name comes from Ralph’s persistent, never-give-up vibe — Ralph may make mistakes, but he keeps going, much like this loop strategy. ([[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Wiggum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][1])

---

### 🔁 How It Works (Core Idea)

* **Looping Mechanism** — At its simplest form, it’s like a `while` loop:

  \```
  while not done:
      run agent on prompt
      check result
  \```

  The agent keeps working *again and again* until it hits completion. ([[Awesome Claude](https://awesomeclaude.ai/ralph-wiggum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][3])

* **Stop Hook** — In implementations like the **Ralph Wiggum plugin** for Claude Code, a “stop hook” intercepts the agent’s attempt to finish and only allows termination if a defined **completion marker** (e.g., “DONE”) is found. Otherwise, it reinjects the prompt so the agent continues iterating. ([[Cyrus](https://www.atcyrus.com/stories/ralph-wiggum-technique-claude-code-autonomous-loops?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][4])

* **Persistence > Perfection** — Rather than perfect on the first try, the agent naturally *fails forward* — each round builds on the last by reading the modified content and improving. ([[Awesome Claude](https://awesomeclaude.ai/ralph-wiggum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][3])

---

### 🛠 Typical Usage

This method is particularly used in **AI-assisted coding** and **automated development tasks**, especially with tools like Claude Code:

✔︎ Large code refactors
✔︎ Migrations or transformations across many files
✔︎ Batch generation (e.g., tests, documentation)
✔︎ Tasks with clear “done” conditions defined by tests or expected outputs ([[Emergent Minds | paddo.dev](https://paddo.dev/blog/ralph-wiggum-autonomous-loops/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][5])

---

### 🧠 Why It Matters

* **Autonomy:** The agent works without constant oversight. ([[Medium](https://jpcaparas.medium.com/ralph-wiggum-explained-the-claude-code-loop-that-keeps-going-3250dcc30809?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][2])
* **Iteration Beats Perfection:** Helps avoid one-shot outputs that stop too early. ([[Awesome Claude](https://awesomeclaude.ai/ralph-wiggum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][3])
* **Feedback Loop Built In:** Each pass refines based on the last. ([[Medium](https://jpcaparas.medium.com/ralph-wiggum-explained-the-claude-code-loop-that-keeps-going-3250dcc30809?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][2])

---

### 🔍 Example (Conceptual)

You might define a task like:
➡️ *“Update all test files to Vitest syntax. Output `<promise>COMPLETED</promise>` when done.”*
The loop runs:

1. Agent attempts
2. Checks for the promise
3. If not found, inject prompt again
4. Repeat until success or max iterations reached ([[Cyrus](https://www.atcyrus.com/stories/ralph-wiggum-technique-claude-code-autonomous-loops?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][4])

---

### ⚠️ Caveats

* If you don’t set strong **success criteria**, the loop can run aimlessly. ([[Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1pxc31u/a_quick_guide_to_ralph_wiggum/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][6])
* Can be **costly** (API calls add up) if left unbounded. ([[zencoder.ai](https://zencoder.ai/blog/wigging-out-controlled-autonomous-loops-in-zenflow?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][7])

---

### 🧠 In Short

The **Ralph Wiggum method** is a **persistent AI looping technique** that keeps an AI agent working on the same task until it genuinely meets your defined success conditions — trading *one-shot perfection* for *iterative convergence*. ([[Medium](https://jpcaparas.medium.com/ralph-wiggum-explained-the-claude-code-loop-that-keeps-going-3250dcc30809?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][2])
